title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: On CdS, a variable-valence Eu center enables a second charge-transfer channel in addition to transfer into the cluster LUMO, whereas Pr, Nd, and Gd do not because the CdS conduction band lies positive of their Ln3+/Ln2+ potentials.
explanation: Photoexcited electrons in Eu52Ni56−xCdx/CdS go both to the cluster LUMO and to Eu3+, generating an in situ Eu2+ center that works with CdS electrons. The review states that electrons are not transferred from CdS to Pr3+, Nd3+, or Gd3+, so those composites remain single-path catalysts and are less active.
scope: Ln52Ni56−xCdx/CdS photocatalytic HER, comparing Eu with Pr, Nd, and Gd.
caveats: The argument depends on the relative positions of the CdS band edge and the Ln3+/Ln2+ couples; it should not be generalized to other semiconductors without those alignments.
